title: jit dep add allows silently creating transitively redundant edges
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2).

`jit dep add` happily creates a transitively redundant edge, but `jit validate` treats transitive-reduction violations as ERRORS — the write succeeds now and the repo fails validation later, wherever the next validate happens to run. In this session, adding `a1b6b3da -> 3d9e9222` silently made the pre-existing `9a7106ae -> 3d9e9222` edge redundant; the violation surfaced inside an UNRELATED issue's code-review gate (which runs jit-validate.sh), costing that issue a review round and a re-run.

The asymmetry is the friction: acyclicity is enforced at write time (cycle detection runs before every dependency operation, INV-DAG-ACYCLIC), while the reduction property is enforced only at read/validate time.

Proposal (either satisfies the intent):
1. `jit dep add` detects that the new edge makes an existing edge redundant (or is itself redundant) and reports which edge, failing unless `--reduce` is passed to drop the now-redundant edge in the same operation; or
2. at minimum, `jit dep add` prints a warning naming the redundant edge so the operator can fix it before a distant validate fails.

Acceptance: adding an edge that shadows an existing direct edge either fails with the offending pair named, auto-reduces under an explicit flag, or warns — a silent success followed by a later validate error is no longer possible.
